title: Zuckerberg details Meta’s personal AI superintelligence strategy
slides: Mark Zuckerberg plans to build AI smarter than humans.
Meta will invest billions in computing infrastructure by 2025.
But a single personal AI assistant, not a one-size-fits-all model.
Your apps could host custom AIs that know your preferences exactly.
The real test: launch your own AI agent by next quarter.
thread_text:
1. Who controls your AI?

Mark Zuckerberg wants your apps to run custom AIs that know your preferences. That means your data isn't just training one model—it's training a thousand.

2. The infrastructure bet

Meta will spend billions on computing by 2025. Every custom AI needs its own brain—and your usage will pay for it.

3. Not one model, but one per user

Your AI assistant won't be generic. It will know your exact habits. The question: who owns that profile?

4. The personalized app takeover

Your apps could host these AIs. Imagine a Facebook that knows your mood, or an Instagram that edits your photos before you ask.

5. Your move: build your own AI agent

Meta says launch yours by next quarter. Take a prompt on ChatGPT and simulate a custom assistant for a task you do daily. Start before the deadline.

instagram.caption:
Meta wants your apps to run custom AIs that know your exact habits, from what you eat to how you edit photos.

Mark Zuckerberg is betting billions on this: not one giant model for everyone, but a personal AI for every user. By 2025, Meta's infrastructure will be built to let each app host a brain tuned just to you.

If you create content, your tools could soon anticipate your edits, your tone, your next post—without you asking.

You can launch your own custom AI agent by next quarter. Pick one repetitive task you do today, and prompt a model to do it for you. Who owns the profile this builds—you or Meta?
